findings.description: When the last attempt fails, the loop hits `break` and the function ends without a return or raise, so `charge` returns None. `settle_invoice` only catches GatewayError, so it then runs `charge.id` on None and raises AttributeError. Any persistent gateway failure now crashes the whole settlement batch, and the invoice is never marked PAYMENT_FAILED. Before this change the GatewayError was caught and recorded.
findings.suggestion: Re-raise the last GatewayError once attempts are exhausted (`raise` instead of `break`), or keep the exception and raise it after the loop.
findings.title: RetryingGateway.charge returns None after retries are exhausted instead of raising

findings.description: Every GatewayError triggers a retry with backoff, including permanent failures such as a card decline or invalid customer. Each such invoice then sleeps through the full backoff (0.5s + 1s by default) before failing, which slows the batch and repeats calls that cannot succeed.
findings.suggestion: Retry only errors marked transient (for example a `retryable` attribute or a subclass), and re-raise the others immediately.
findings.title: All GatewayErrors are retried, including non-transient ones
